He who was there at the same time, at the very same place, he is not able to believe the statement of his brother, that it was Vlatko who was there. Why would the Court believe him? I believe that this seriously brings into question this particular statement. There was shooting taking place from Vlatko's house that day and it was only logical to hold the owner of that house accountable for that. And now another question that remains hanging in the air all the time. Why would these witnesses charge Vlatko Kupreskic with that? Why would they present false accusations, et cetera? Yesterday the Prosecutor said that conspiracy was not proven of witnesses who had the intention of falsely accusing the persons accused who are sitting here. I believe that the answer is simpler than that. It is revenge. These witnesses of the Prosecution come to this Tribunal to avenge their dead. They are not coming to seek justice. That's a simple motive. In a way, it is understandable. They want to take revenge on their Croat neighbours. That is unimportant now -- I mean, whether it is Vlatko or some other neighbour. So that is the answer to "how come?" That is to say the wish for revenge overrode the wish for justice. That is the motive that could have prevailed. However, in spite of all of that, we assessed Witness Q's testimony even if it were to be assumed that everything happened exactly the way he had said it did. We asked an expert, Professor Wagenaar, whether it was possible from a 50 metre or so distance to recognise a person whom one knew. We heard Professor Wagenaar's testimony. The answer is that such recognition would be absolutely unreliable and unacceptable from a scientific point of view. So what can we say about the evidence concerning counts 12 through 15 of the indictment? Even if the offence had not proven anything else, if all the options presented by the Prosecutor were to be accepted, the only thing that would remain as evidence against Vlatko Kupreskic would be the testimony of Witness Q, a testimony that is scientifically unacceptable. For all these reasons, the Defence for the accused Vlatko Kupreskic believes that the presented Defence evidence has totally rebutted the allegations from the indictment, and that the accused Vlatko Kupreskic has to be acquitted of charges on these counts. Finally, you will allow me to point out a very illogical point regarding the accusation levelled against Vlatko Kupreskic, and I am certain that the Court noticed this as well. And I am sure that this requires special explanation. Namely, the indictment states that at this critical moment, together with Fata and Dzenana Pezer, a woman had been hit and wounded too. As for the wounding of this woman, Vlatko Kupreskic is not being charged with anything. Why would there be such a situation in the indictment, that Vlatko Kupreskic should be forgiven to grave crimes? The point is that there is no woman who was wounded. It is Court Witness CF who was wounded. That is a fact that no one has denied. The Prosecutor is not charging Vlatko Kupreskic with the wounding of Witness CF for only one reason. He would have to prove that CF was wounded at the same place, at the same time when Fata and Dzenana Pezer were shot and wounded. Then he would have to call Witness CF, and that would bring down the accusation, the indictment, because it would be ascertained that this is a completely different place. And how could that be the responsibility of Vlatko Kupreskic? We are aware of the fact that the Prosecutor has the right to rebut what the Defence is saying, but I am sure that the Trial Chamber is going to appreciate this fact when considering counts 12 through 15. So the final and only proposal of the Defence is that the accused Vlatko Kupreskic be acquitted with regard to all counts in the indictment, because it has not been proven that he committed the crimes that he has been charged with in the indictment. I also wish to note that today the Defence presented to the Registry a request for the provisional release of Vlatko Kupreskic, believing that there are special reasons for that, in terms of Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. We have submitted this request in writing, so I shall not elaborate on it right now, but I do ask the Court, in the light of all those reasons and all the other circumstances involved in this case, to make it possible for Vlatko Kupreskic to remain at liberty until a final ruling is made by this Court. I thank you.
